Now I have a thorough understanding of both the UNS domain and your project context. Let me compile the comprehensive technical summary.

---

## Unified Namespace (UNS) for OT / Industrial Data -- Technical Research Summary

---

### 1. What Exactly Is a UNS -- The Core Concept

A Unified Namespace is **not a product or a database**. It is an **architectural design pattern** that creates a single, event-driven data layer representing the current state of an entire industrial operation. Every system -- OT devices, SCADA, MES, ERP, analytics platforms -- publishes and consumes data through this shared layer instead of maintaining point-to-point integrations.

The core mechanics:

- **A central message broker** (typically MQTT) acts as the hub. Every data producer publishes to it; every consumer subscribes from it.
- **A hierarchical topic namespace** organizes all data by physical and logical location, following ISA-95 equipment hierarchy conventions.
- **The namespace is a "live mirror" of the physical world.** It holds the last known value of every data point. It is not a historian -- it is the current state, continuously updated.
- **It replaces the Purdue Model's layer-by-layer communication.** Instead of Level 0 talking only to Level 1, which talks to Level 2, etc., any level can publish to or subscribe from the UNS directly.

The key insight: in traditional architectures, connecting N systems requires up to N*(N-1)/2 point-to-point integrations. A UNS reduces this to N connections (each system connects only to the broker). This is the "hub and spoke" pattern applied to industrial data.

A UNS is protocol-agnostic in theory (OPC UA can also serve as the backbone), but MQTT has emerged as the dominant implementation protocol due to its lightweight publish/subscribe model, hierarchical topic structure, retained messages (for "current state"), and Last Will and Testament feature.

Sources: [HiveMQ UNS Essentials](https://www.hivemq.com/mqtt/unified-namespace-uns-essentials-iiot-industry-40/), [Cedalo - What is UNS](https://cedalo.com/blog/unified-namespace-uns/), [Inductive Automation - UNS Defined](https://inductiveautomation.com/resources/article/uns-unified-namespace), [United Manufacturing Hub](https://www.umh.app/product/unified-namespace)

---

### 2. Typical Topic Hierarchy Structure (MQTT-Based)

MQTT topics use forward-slash-delimited hierarchical paths. The UNS convention maps physical and organizational structure into this hierarchy, typically following ISA-95 equipment levels.

**General pattern:**

```
{Enterprise}/{Site}/{Area}/{ProductionLine}/{WorkCell}/{Equipment}/{DataCategory}
```

**Concrete example from an automotive manufacturer:**

```
AutoIndustries/Munich/PressShopArea/DoorPressProductionLine/FormingWorkCell/MechanicalPress/State
AutoIndustries/Munich/PressShopArea/DoorPressProductionLine/FormingWorkCell/MechanicalPress/Parameters
AutoIndustries/Munich/PressShopArea/DoorPressProductionLine/FormingWorkCell/MechanicalPress/Alarms
```

**What each level represents:**

| Level | ISA-95 Equivalent | Purpose | Example |
|-------|-------------------|---------|---------|
| 1 | Enterprise | Top-level organization | `AcmeEnergy` |
| 2 | Site | Geographic/operational facility | `PermianBasin` |
| 3 | Area | Functional subdivision | `NorthField` |
| 4 | Production Line | Process or production stream | `Pad-12` |
| 5 | Work Cell | Smallest groupable unit | `Well-77` |
| 6 | Equipment / Asset | Individual device | `ESP-01` |
| 7 | Data Category | Type of data | `telemetry`, `alarms`, `state` |

**MQTT wildcard subscriptions** make the hierarchy powerful:

- `AcmeEnergy/PermianBasin/+/+/+/+/alarms` -- all alarms across the Permian Basin
- `AcmeEnergy/PermianBasin/NorthField/#` -- everything from the North Field
- `+/+/+/+/+/+/state` -- all equipment states across the entire enterprise

**Additional namespace branches for IT systems:**

```
AutoIndustries/Munich/ERP/Production/Order
AutoIndustries/Munich/MES/Quality
AutoIndustries/Munich/PressShopArea/DoorPressProductionLine/Edge/ScrapCount
```

The UMH (United Manufacturing Hub) implementation adds explicit versioning and schema markers:

```
umh/v1/{enterprise}/{site}/{area}/{productionLine}/{workCell}/{originID}/{_schema}
```

Where `_schema` can be `_historian`, `_analytics`, or `_local`, determining how the message is routed and persisted downstream.

Sources: [HiveMQ - UNS Semantic Data Hierarchy](https://www.hivemq.com/blog/uns-semantic-data-hierarchy-mqtt-explained-with-example/), [FlowFuse - Designing Topic Hierarchy](https://flowfuse.com/blog/2025/01/designing-topic-hierarchy-for-your-uns/), [UMH Data Modeling](https://learn.umh.app/lesson/data-modeling-in-the-unified-namespace-mqtt-kafka/)

---

### 3. How ISA-95 Maps into UNS Topic Structures

ISA-95 (also called the Purdue Model in its networking form) defines a 5-level hierarchy for manufacturing operations. The UNS maps these levels directly into topic path segments:

| ISA-95 Level | Level # | UNS Topic Role | Example Topic Segment |
|--------------|---------|-----------------|----------------------|
| Enterprise | 4 | Root topic | `/enterprise/` |
| Site | 3-4 | Geographic grouping | `/enterprise/site/` |
| Area | 3 | Functional zone | `/enterprise/site/area/` |
| Line / Process Cell | 2 | Production unit | `/.../productionLine/` |
| Work Cell / Unit | 1-2 | Smallest operational group | `/.../workCell/` |
| Equipment / Control Module | 0-1 | Individual asset | `/.../equipment/` |

**ISA-95 levels mapped to MQTT topic function:**

```
Level 4 (Enterprise/ERP):  AcmeEnergy/ERP/inventory/overview
Level 3 (MES/MOM):         AcmeEnergy/PermianBasin/MES/productionOrder
Level 2 (Supervisory):     AcmeEnergy/PermianBasin/NorthField/supervisor/alerts
Level 1 (Control/PLC):     REDACTED
Level 0 (Sensors):         REDACTED
```

The critical architectural shift is that in the traditional Purdue Model, data flows sequentially between adjacent levels (Level 0 to Level 1 to Level 2, etc.). In a UNS, any level publishes directly to the namespace, and any level subscribes directly. The hierarchy is retained in the topic naming, but communication is no longer constrained to layer-by-layer traversal.

**Practical nuance from your project:** Your ARCHITECTURE.md already defines an ISA-95 hierarchy (Enterprise/Site/Area/Cell/Equipment) that maps directly to UNS topic generation. The `UNS Topic Builder` in your pipeline produces topics like:

```
acme-energy/permian/north/pad-12/well/e-77/telemetry
```

This is exactly the ISA-95-to-UNS mapping pattern used in production systems.

Sources: [HiveMQ - Smart Manufacturing Using ISA95, Sparkplug and UNS](https://www.hivemq.com/resources/smart-manufacturing-using-isa95-mqtt-sparkplug-and-uns/), [FlowFuse - Designing Topic Hierarchy](https://flowfuse.com/blog/2025/01/designing-topic-hierarchy-for-your-uns/), [Corso Systems - ISA-95 and Sparkplug B](https://corsosystems.com/posts/using-isa-95-and-sparkplug-b-together)

---

### 4. Payload Conventions -- What a UNS Message Looks Like

There is no single enforced standard, but strong conventions have emerged. Two primary approaches exist: **plain MQTT with JSON payloads** and **Sparkplug B with Protobuf payloads**.

#### 4a. Plain MQTT / JSON Payload (Most Common for Getting Started)

**Minimal sensor reading:**

```json
{
  "timestamp": "2025-01-15T14:32:00.000Z",
  "value": 25.5,
  "unit": "Celsius",
  "quality": "Good"
}
```

**Richer telemetry payload (typical convention):**

```json
{
  "timestamp": "2025-01-15T14:32:00.000Z",
  "metrics": {
    "tubing_pressure_psi": 1250.3,
    "casing_pressure_psi": 890.1,
    "oil_rate_bpd": 320.5,
    "water_cut_pct": 45.2,
    "esp_frequency_hz": 55.0,
    "esp_motor_temp_f": 285.0,
    "esp_current_amps": 32.5
  },
  "quality": "Good",
  "source": "CygNet-SCADA",
  "equipment_id": "ESP-77"
}
```

**UMH _historian format (timestamp as Unix milliseconds):**

```json
{
  "timestamp_ms": 1680698839098,
  "tubing_pressure": 1250.3,
  "casing_pressure": 890.1,
  "motor_temperature": 285.0
}
```

**Key payload conventions:**

| Field | Convention | Notes |
|-------|-----------|-------|
| `timestamp` | ISO 8601 UTC or Unix epoch milliseconds | Time of data acquisition, not receipt |
| `value` / `metrics` | Numeric or structured object | Single value or batch of related measurements |
| `unit` / `uom` | String, standardized | Always include; standardize across enterprise |
| `quality` | Enum: `Good`, `Bad`, `Uncertain` | OPC UA quality model commonly borrowed |
| `source` | String identifier | Originating system for lineage |

**Batched metrics (for report-by-exception with historical backfill):**

```json
{
  "timestamp_ms": 1680698839098,
  "batch": [
    {"timestamp_ms": 1680698835000, "value": 1248.1},
    {"timestamp_ms": 1680698837000, "value": 1249.7},
    {"timestamp_ms": 1680698839000, "value": 1250.3}
  ]
}
```

#### 4b. Envelope Pattern (What Your Project Generates)

Your project's `UNSEnvelope` model wraps the canonical payload with context -- this is the recommended enterprise pattern:

```json
{
  "topic": "acme-energy/permian/north/pad-12/well/e-77/telemetry",
  "event_time": "2025-01-15T14:32:00Z",
  "payload": { "...canonical telemetry..." },
  "context": {
    "enterprise": "AcmeEnergy",
    "site": "Permian",
    "area": "North",
    "cell": "Pad-12",
    "equipment_class": "Well",
    "equipment_id": "E-77"
  },
  "meta": { "...lineage records..." },
  "data_quality": { "rating": "Good", "flags": [] }
}
```

Sources: [FlowFuse - UNS Data Modelling](https://flowfuse.com/blog/2023/12/unified-namespace-data-modelling/), [Cedalo - UNS MQTT Implementation](https://cedalo.com/blog/uns-mqtt-implementation/), [UMH Data Modeling](https://learn.umh.app/lesson/data-modeling-in-the-unified-namespace-mqtt-kafka/)

---

### 5. The Role of Sparkplug B Specification

Sparkplug B is an Eclipse Foundation specification that adds structure, state management, and interoperability guarantees on top of plain MQTT. It does not replace MQTT -- it defines **how** to use MQTT for industrial IoT.

#### Topic Namespace

Sparkplug mandates a fixed topic format:

```
spBv1.0/{group_id}/{message_type}/{edge_node_id}/[device_id]
```

**Message types:**

| Type | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `NBIRTH` | Edge node birth certificate -- declares all metrics, types, initial values |
| `NDEATH` | Edge node death certificate -- signals node disconnection |
| `DBIRTH` | Device birth certificate -- declares device metrics |
| `DDEATH` | Device death certificate |
| `NDATA` | Node data -- changed metrics only (report-by-exception) |
| `DDATA` | Device data -- changed metrics only |
| `NCMD` | Command to a node |
| `DCMD` | Command to a device |
| `STATE` | Critical application state (e.g., primary SCADA host status) |

#### Payload Format (Protobuf, Not JSON)

Sparkplug uses Google Protocol Buffers for compact binary serialization:

```json
// JSON representation of a Sparkplug B NBIRTH payload:
{
  "timestamp": 1486144502122,
  "metrics": [
    {
      "name": "Tubing Pressure",
      "alias": 1,
      "timestamp": 1479123452194,
      "dataType": "Float",
      "value": 1250.3,
      "is_historical": false,
      "is_transient": false,
      "is_null": false,
      "properties": {
        "engUnit": {"type": "String", "value": "psi"},
        "engLow": {"type": "Float", "value": 0.0},
        "engHigh": {"type": "Float", "value": 5000.0}
      }
    },
    {
      "name": "Motor Temperature",
      "alias": 2,
      "timestamp": 1479123452194,
      "dataType": "Float",
      "value": 285.0
    }
  ],
  "seq": 0
}
```

After the BIRTH message, subsequent NDATA/DDATA messages use **aliases instead of names** to reduce payload size:

```json
{
  "timestamp": 1486144562122,
  "metrics": [
    {"alias": 1, "timestamp": 1486144562000, "dataType": "Float", "value": 1252.1}
  ],
  "seq": 3
}
```

#### How Sparkplug B Differs from Plain MQTT

| Feature | Plain MQTT | Sparkplug B |
|---------|-----------|-------------|
| Payload format | Free-form (usually JSON) | Protobuf (defined schema) |
| State management | None built-in | Birth/Death certificates |
| Metric discovery | Manual / out-of-band | Automatic via BIRTH messages |
| Data types | Implicit | Explicit (Int32, Float, Boolean, etc.) |
| Report-by-exception | Application-level | Protocol-level with sequence tracking |
| Topic structure | Free-form | Mandated namespace |
| Bandwidth efficiency | Moderate (JSON text) | High (binary + aliases) |
| Interoperability | Low (custom schemas) | High (any Sparkplug-aware consumer) |

#### The ISA-95 Mapping Problem with Sparkplug

Sparkplug provides only three customizable topic segments: `group_id`, `edge_node_id`, `device_id`. ISA-95 needs 5+ levels. Two workarounds exist:

**Parris Method** -- embed hierarchy in group_id using a delimiter:

```
spBv1.0/AcmeEnergy:Permian:NorthField:Pad12/DDATA/PLC-01/ESP-77
```

**Recommended approach** -- convert Sparkplug topics to vanilla MQTT topics at the broker level, then build the ISA-95 hierarchy in the plain MQTT namespace. This avoids forcing the equipment model into Sparkplug's constrained topic structure.

Sources: [HiveMQ - Sparkplug Payload Structures](https://www.hivemq.com/blog/mqtt-payload-structures-iiot/), [Eclipse Sparkplug 3.0 Spec](https://www.eclipse.org/tahu/spec/sparkplug_spec.pdf), [Corso Systems - ISA-95 and Sparkplug B](https://corsosystems.com/posts/using-isa-95-and-sparkplug-b-together), [Canary Labs - Sparkplug](https://blog.canarylabs.com/get-started-with-mqtt-sparkplug)

---

### 6. Key Architectural Patterns

#### 6a. Publish / Subscribe

The fundamental pattern. Publishers and subscribers are completely decoupled:

- **Publishers** (PLCs, SCADA gateways, edge devices) send data to topic paths. They do not know or care who is listening.
- **Subscribers** (dashboards, historians, analytics engines, MES) subscribe to topic patterns. They do not know or care who is publishing.
- **The broker** handles routing. This is the only integration point.

This means adding a new consumer (e.g., a machine learning pipeline) requires zero changes to any existing publisher.

#### 6b. Report-by-Exception (RBE)

Data is published only when a value changes, not on a fixed poll interval. This is fundamental to both Sparkplug B and efficient UNS operation.

**How it works:**

1. On connection, a BIRTH message publishes all current metric values (the "full state snapshot").
2. After that, only changed values are published.
3. The broker retains the last message per topic (`retained` flag), so new subscribers immediately get current state.
4. Sparkplug adds sequence numbers to detect gaps (missed messages).

**Trade-off:** Tags that legitimately do not change for long periods may appear "stale" to monitoring systems. Solutions include periodic heartbeat publishes or configuring stale-detection thresholds.

#### 6c. Birth and Death Certificates

This pattern solves a critical problem: **how does a consumer know what data a device provides, and whether the device is currently online?**

**Birth certificate (NBIRTH / DBIRTH):**

- Published when a device connects or reconnects
- Contains the complete list of metrics with names, data types, initial values, and engineering units
- Enables auto-discovery -- a new SCADA application can subscribe to `spBv1.0/+/DBIRTH/#` and automatically learn every device and metric in the system

**Death certificate (NDEATH / DDEATH):**

- Published when a device disconnects
- Uses MQTT's **Last Will and Testament (LWT)** feature: the death message is registered with the broker at connection time, and the broker publishes it automatically if the client disconnects unexpectedly (network failure, power loss)
- All subscribers instantly know the device is offline and can mark its data as stale/uncertain

**State awareness flow:**

```
1. Device connects    -> Broker publishes NBIRTH (all metrics + initial values)
2. Value changes      -> Device publishes NDATA (changed metrics only)
3. Device disconnects -> Broker publishes NDEATH (via LWT)
4. Device reconnects  -> Broker publishes NBIRTH (full state refresh)
```

Sources: [Canary Labs - Sparkplug RBE](https://blog.canarylabs.com/get-started-with-mqtt-sparkplug), [HiveMQ - Sparkplug Architecture](https://www.hivemq.com/blog/sparkplug-essentials-part-2-architecture/), [Inductive Automation Forum - RBE Tag Staleness](https://forum.inductiveautomation.com/t/mqtt-tags-go-stale-due-to-uns-report-by-exception/86590)

---

### 7. Contextualization -- Mapping Raw SCADA Tags into UNS Topics

This is the central problem your `scada_harmonization` project addresses. Raw SCADA tags carry no inherent context about where they sit in the organizational hierarchy.

#### The Problem: Raw Tags Have No Context

A typical SCADA system has flat, cryptic tag names:

```
45TT236          (plant 45, temperature transmitter, loop 236)
WELL_E77_TBG_P   (well E-77, tubing pressure)
E77.ESP.MotorTemp (dot-separated, camelCase)
csg_press_kpa    (snake_case, non-standard units)
```

These carry meaning to the person who configured them, but they are opaque to any system consuming them for cross-site analytics.

#### The Solution: A Contextualization Layer

Contextualization is the process of extracting or enriching these raw tags with:

1. **ISA-95 identity** -- which enterprise, site, area, cell, and equipment this tag belongs to
2. **Semantic meaning** -- what physical measurement this tag represents (tubing pressure, motor temperature, flow rate)
3. **Unit standardization** -- converting to a common unit system
4. **Quality assessment** -- flagging suspect or out-of-range values

#### Where Contextualization Happens

In a UNS architecture, contextualization typically occurs at the **edge gateway** or in a **transformation layer** between the raw data source and the UNS broker:

```
PLC / RTU (raw tags)
    |
    v
Edge Gateway / Adapter
    - Parses tag naming conventions
    - Maps tag to ISA-95 hierarchy
    - Converts units
    - Adds metadata (timestamp, quality, source)
    |
    v
MQTT Broker (UNS)
    - Topic: acme-energy/permian/north/pad-12/well/e-77/telemetry
    - Payload: standardized JSON with context
```

#### Concrete Mapping Example

**Raw SCADA tag from CygNet-style source:**

```
Tag:    WELL_E77_TBG_PRESS
Value:  8618.7
Unit:   kPa
Status: P
```

**Contextualized UNS output:**

```
Topic: acme-energy/permian/north/pad-12/well/e-77/telemetry

Payload:
{
  "timestamp": "2025-01-15T14:32:00Z",
  "tubing_pressure_psi": 1250.3,
  "quality": "Good",
  "lineage": {
    "tubing_pressure_psi": {
      "source_key": "WELL_E77_TBG_PRESS",
      "original_value": 8618.7,
      "conversion": "kPa_to_psi"
    }
  }
}
```

**Two-tier namespace approach (recommended):**

Some architectures maintain both a raw namespace and a contextualized namespace:

```
_raw/cygnet/WELL_E77_TBG_PRESS        <- raw data, unprocessed, ingested immediately
acme-energy/permian/north/.../telemetry <- contextualized, standardized, enterprise-ready
```

The raw namespace allows data collection from day one while the contextualization model is still being refined.

Sources: [HiveMQ - Designing UNS Semantic Hierarchy](https://www.hivemq.com/blog/designing-your-uns-semantic-information-hierarchy/), [FlowFuse - UNS Data Modelling](https://flowfuse.com/blog/2023/12/unified-namespace-data-modelling/), [i-flow - SCADA in the UNS](https://i-flow.io/en/ressources/scada-in-the-unified-namespace-uns-new-role-in-industrial-iot/)

---

### 8. Real-World UNS Topic Tree for Upstream Oil & Gas

While published examples are scarce for oil & gas specifically (most public UNS documentation uses manufacturing examples), the ISA-95 hierarchy maps naturally to upstream operations. Based on the conventions established above and oil & gas domain structure, here is a realistic topic tree:

```
acme-energy/                                          # Enterprise
  permian-basin/                                      # Site
    north-field/                                      # Area
      pad-12/                                         # Cell (well pad)
        well/                                         # Equipment Class
          e-77/                                       # Equipment ID
            telemetry/                                # Real-time measurements
              tubing-pressure
              casing-pressure
              oil-rate
              water-cut
              gas-rate
              wellhead-temperature
            status/                                   # Operating state
            alarms/                                   # Alarm events
          e-78/
            telemetry/
            status/
        esp/                                          # Equipment Class
          esp-77/                                     # Equipment ID
            telemetry/
              motor-temperature
              intake-pressure
              discharge-pressure
              vibration
              frequency
              current
              power
            status/                                   # running, tripped, idle
            alarms/                                   # high-temp, overcurrent
            performance/                              # calculated KPIs
              pump-efficiency
              head-curve-deviation
          esp-78/
            telemetry/
            status/
        separator/
          sep-12a/
            telemetry/
              oil-out-rate
              water-out-rate
              gas-out-rate
              level
              pressure
              temperature
            status/
      pad-13/
        well/
          e-80/
            ...
    south-field/                                      # Area
      pad-20/
        ...
  eagle-ford/                                         # Site
    central-block/                                    # Area
      ...
  _enterprise/                                        # Enterprise-level systems
    erp/
      production-accounting/
      lease-operating-expense/
    scada-historian/
      archive-status/
    analytics/
      field-decline-curves/
      esp-health-scores/
```

**Key design decisions for oil & gas:**

- **Pad as Cell:** A well pad is the natural equivalent of an ISA-95 work cell -- it is the smallest unit that groups related equipment.
- **Equipment class as a level:** Separating `well/`, `esp/`, `separator/` under a pad allows subscribing to all ESPs across a field with `acme-energy/permian-basin/north-field/+/esp/#`.
- **Telemetry vs. status vs. alarms:** Separate data categories as sub-topics so consumers can subscribe to exactly what they need.
- **Enterprise systems as sibling branches:** ERP, analytics, and historian data live in the same namespace but under clearly separated branches.

Sources: [HiveMQ - Oil & Gas Digital Transformation](https://www.hivemq.com/blog/digital-transformation-oil-gas-uns-mqtt-distributed-data-intelligence/), [HiveMQ - Upstream Oil & Gas Case Study](https://www.hivemq.com/case-studies/upstream-oil-and-gas/), [EMQ - MQTT in Oil & Gas](https://www.emqx.com/en/blog/application-of-mqtt-protocol-in-oil-and-gas-industry)

---

### 9. Common Pitfalls When Implementing UNS

**1. No clear business objective.** The most common failure mode. Teams implement a UNS because it is trendy without defining what business outcomes it should enable. Without a "why," initial enthusiasm fades.

**2. Lack of data governance.** Without central specifications for topic naming, payload schemas, and data ownership, the namespace degenerates into a "chaotic namespace." Different teams create inconsistent topic structures, redundant data, and incompatible payload formats. You need someone (or a team) who owns the data model.

**3. Trying to harmonize OT data without standardization at source level.** Factories and fields have historically grown, proprietary data structures with inconsistent naming. Without technical harmonization (uniform payload formats, consistent topic mapping), the UNS becomes a dumping ground. This is exactly the problem your harmonization service solves.

**4. Ignoring security from the start.** Once data is in the UNS, it is accessible to all subscribers. Access control, encryption (TLS), and authentication must be part of the initial design, not bolted on later.

**5. Forcing ISA-95 mapping into Sparkplug B's limited topic structure.** Sparkplug only provides three customizable topic segments. Embedding a 5+ level ISA-95 hierarchy using delimiters creates technical debt and parsing complexity for every consumer.

**6. Not handling "brownfield" integration.** Most industrial environments have legacy PLCs, RTUs, and protocols (Modbus, OPC DA) that cannot natively publish MQTT. Edge gateways are required, and their selection, configuration, and maintenance are a significant project in themselves.

**7. Over-engineering the topic structure before collecting any data.** Some teams spend months designing the "perfect" namespace before publishing a single message. The recommended approach: start with a raw namespace, collect data immediately, and refine the contextualized namespace iteratively.

**8. Confusing UNS with a historian or data lake.** The UNS is a real-time current-state layer. It is not a replacement for time-series storage. Historians, data lakes, and analytics systems should subscribe to the UNS and persist data according to their own retention needs.

**9. Underestimating organizational change.** UNS requires cross-functional collaboration between OT, IT, and data engineering teams. Naming conventions and data ownership disputes are often harder to resolve than technical challenges.

Sources: [i-flow - Why UNS Projects Fail](https://i-flow.io/en/ressources/6-organizational-mistakes-why-unified-namespace-uns-projects-fail-in-manufacturing-companies/), [i-flow - Lessons from the Data Lake Hype](https://i-flow.io/en/ressources/unified-namespace-lessons-from-the-data-lake-hype/), [Automation World - UNS Real-World Challenges](https://www.automationworld.com/factory/iiot/article/33016191/unified-namespace-real-world-applications-and-challenges)

---

### 10. File-Based / Batch Simulation of UNS Concepts

Your project is already a demonstration of this approach. A file-based simulation can faithfully represent all the core UNS concepts without requiring a live MQTT broker. Here is how each concept maps:

| UNS Concept | Live MQTT Implementation | File-Based Equivalent |
|-------------|------------------------|-----------------------|
| **Topic namespace** | MQTT topic string | Generated topic path in output JSON (your `UNSEnvelope.topic`) |
| **Publish** | `client.publish(topic, payload)` | Write a JSON line to `canonical.jsonl` with topic + payload |
| **Subscribe** | `client.subscribe("acme/+/+/esp/#")` | Filter/grep output JSONL by topic pattern |
| **Retained message (current state)** | Broker stores last message per topic | Python dictionary keyed by topic path (last-write-wins) |
| **Report-by-exception** | Only publish on value change | Compare incoming value against last-known value in state dict; only write if changed |
| **Birth certificate** | NBIRTH with all metrics | Initial "full snapshot" record per device in output |
| **Death certificate** | NDEATH on disconnect | Sentinel record with `"status": "offline"` and timestamp |
| **Quality flags** | `is_null`, `quality` in payload | Your `DataQuality` model (Good/Suspect/Bad + flags) |
| **Dead letter** | Error topic or separate queue | Your `dead_letter.jsonl` |
| **Wildcard subscription** | `+` and `#` in topic filter | Regex or glob matching on topic strings in output |

**Implementation pattern using a Python dictionary as an in-memory UNS:**

```python
class InMemoryUNS:
    """Simulates a UNS broker as a Python dictionary."""
    
    def __init__(self):
        self.state: dict[str, dict] = {}         # topic -> last payload (retained)
        self.subscribers: dict[str, list] = {}     # pattern -> [callback, ...]
        self.history: list[dict] = []              # ordered event log
    
    def publish(self, topic: str, payload: dict):
        """Simulate MQTT publish with retain."""
        self.state[topic] = payload                # retained message
        self.history.append({"topic": topic, "payload": payload})
        for pattern, callbacks in self.subscribers.items():
            if topic_matches(pattern, topic):
                for cb in callbacks:
                    cb(topic, payload)
    
    def subscribe(self, pattern: str, callback):
        """Simulate MQTT subscribe with wildcards."""
        self.subscribers.setdefault(pattern, []).append(callback)
        # Deliver retained messages for matching topics
        for topic, payload in self.state.items():
            if topic_matches(pattern, topic):
                callback(topic, payload)
    
    def get_current_state(self, topic: str) -> dict | None:
        """Get retained message for a topic."""
        return self.state.get(topic)
    
    def export_to_jsonl(self, path: str):
        """Persist the event log to file."""
        with open(path, "w") as f:
            for event in self.history:
                f.write(json.dumps(event) + "\n")
```

**What your project already demonstrates:**

Your pipeline (fixture files -> adapters -> canonical model -> UNS envelope -> JSONL output) is functionally equivalent to:

1. **Ingestion** = receiving published messages from multiple SCADA sources
2. **Adapters** = edge gateway contextualization (raw tags -> ISA-95 hierarchy)
3. **Canonical model** = enforcing the payload schema contract
4. **UNS Envelope** = producing the message that would be published to the broker
5. **JSONL output** = the "broker's" persistent event log
6. **Dead letter** = the error/rejection queue

To make the UNS simulation more explicit, you could add:
- A state dictionary that maintains "current value" per topic (simulating MQTT retained messages)
- A report-by-exception filter that compares each incoming value against the retained state and only emits if changed
- A birth/death event generator that produces initial full-state snapshots and offline sentinel records

Sources: [GitHub - mkashwin/unifiednamespace](https://github.com/mkashwin/unifiednamespace), [Cedalo - UNS MQTT Implementation](https://cedalo.com/blog/uns-mqtt-implementation/)

---

### Summary: How This Maps to Your SCADA Harmonization Project

Your existing architecture at `REDACTED` is already implementing the core of what a UNS contextualization layer does:

| UNS Function | Your Implementation |
|---|---|
| Source ingestion | Multi-adapter system (CygNet, Wonderware, Ignition) with discriminated union detection |
| Contextualization | Adapter layer extracts ISA-95 identity from raw tag naming |
| Schema enforcement | Strict Pydantic canonical model with constrained types |
| Topic generation | `UNS Topic Builder` derives deterministic topic paths from ISA-95 fields |
| Payload standardization | Unit conversion, timestamp normalization, status enum mapping |
| Quality assessment | `DataQuality` scorer with Good/Suspect/Bad ratings |

The project effectively implements the **edge contextualization gateway** portion of a UNS architecture, which is the hardest and most valuable part to get right. The remaining step to make it a full UNS demonstration would be adding the in-memory state management (retained messages, report-by-exception filtering) and birth/death certificate generation described in section 10 above.

Now I have a thorough understanding of both the UNS domain and your project context. Let me compile the comprehensive technical summary.

---

## Unified Namespace (UNS) for OT / Industrial Data -- Technical Research Summary

---

### 1. What Exactly Is a UNS -- The Core Concept

A Unified Namespace is **not a product or a database**. It is an **architectural design pattern** that creates a single, event-driven data layer representing the current state of an entire industrial operation. Every system -- OT devices, SCADA, MES, ERP, analytics platforms -- publishes and consumes data through this shared layer instead of maintaining point-to-point integrations.

The core mechanics:

- **A central message broker** (typically MQTT) acts as the hub. Every data producer publishes to it; every consumer subscribes from it.
- **A hierarchical topic namespace** organizes all data by physical and logical location, following ISA-95 equipment hierarchy conventions.
- **The namespace is a "live mirror" of the physical world.** It holds the last known value of every data point. It is not a historian -- it is the current state, continuously updated.
- **It replaces the Purdue Model's layer-by-layer communication.** Instead of Level 0 talking only to Level 1, which talks to Level 2, etc., any level can publish to or subscribe from the UNS directly.

The key insight: in traditional architectures, connecting N systems requires up to N*(N-1)/2 point-to-point integrations. A UNS reduces this to N connections (each system connects only to the broker). This is the "hub and spoke" pattern applied to industrial data.

A UNS is protocol-agnostic in theory (OPC UA can also serve as the backbone), but MQTT has emerged as the dominant implementation protocol due to its lightweight publish/subscribe model, hierarchical topic structure, retained messages (for "current state"), and Last Will and Testament feature.

Sources: [HiveMQ UNS Essentials](https://www.hivemq.com/mqtt/unified-namespace-uns-essentials-iiot-industry-40/), [Cedalo - What is UNS](https://cedalo.com/blog/unified-namespace-uns/), [Inductive Automation - UNS Defined](https://inductiveautomation.com/resources/article/uns-unified-namespace), [United Manufacturing Hub](https://www.umh.app/product/unified-namespace)

---

### 2. Typical Topic Hierarchy Structure (MQTT-Based)

MQTT topics use forward-slash-delimited hierarchical paths. The UNS convention maps physical and organizational structure into this hierarchy, typically following ISA-95 equipment levels.

**General pattern:**

```
{Enterprise}/{Site}/{Area}/{ProductionLine}/{WorkCell}/{Equipment}/{DataCategory}
```

**Concrete example from an automotive manufacturer:**

```
AutoIndustries/Munich/PressShopArea/DoorPressProductionLine/FormingWorkCell/MechanicalPress/State
AutoIndustries/Munich/PressShopArea/DoorPressProductionLine/FormingWorkCell/MechanicalPress/Parameters
AutoIndustries/Munich/PressShopArea/DoorPressProductionLine/FormingWorkCell/MechanicalPress/Alarms
```

**What each level represents:**

| Level | ISA-95 Equivalent | Purpose | Example |
|-------|-------------------|---------|---------|
| 1 | Enterprise | Top-level organization | `AcmeEnergy` |
| 2 | Site | Geographic/operational facility | `PermianBasin` |
| 3 | Area | Functional subdivision | `NorthField` |
| 4 | Production Line | Process or production stream | `Pad-12` |
| 5 | Work Cell | Smallest groupable unit | `Well-77` |
| 6 | Equipment / Asset | Individual device | `ESP-01` |
| 7 | Data Category | Type of data | `telemetry`, `alarms`, `state` |

**MQTT wildcard subscriptions** make the hierarchy powerful:

- `AcmeEnergy/PermianBasin/+/+/+/+/alarms` -- all alarms across the Permian Basin
- `AcmeEnergy/PermianBasin/NorthField/#` -- everything from the North Field
- `+/+/+/+/+/+/state` -- all equipment states across the entire enterprise

**Additional namespace branches for IT systems:**

```
AutoIndustries/Munich/ERP/Production/Order
AutoIndustries/Munich/MES/Quality
AutoIndustries/Munich/PressShopArea/DoorPressProductionLine/Edge/ScrapCount
```

The UMH (United Manufacturing Hub) implementation adds explicit versioning and schema markers:

```
umh/v1/{enterprise}/{site}/{area}/{productionLine}/{workCell}/{originID}/{_schema}
```

Where `_schema` can be `_historian`, `_analytics`, or `_local`, determining how the message is routed and persisted downstream.

Sources: [HiveMQ - UNS Semantic Data Hierarchy](https://www.hivemq.com/blog/uns-semantic-data-hierarchy-mqtt-explained-with-example/), [FlowFuse - Designing Topic Hierarchy](https://flowfuse.com/blog/2025/01/designing-topic-hierarchy-for-your-uns/), [UMH Data Modeling](https://learn.umh.app/lesson/data-modeling-in-the-unified-namespace-mqtt-kafka/)

---

### 3. How ISA-95 Maps into UNS Topic Structures

ISA-95 (also called the Purdue Model in its networking form) defines a 5-level hierarchy for manufacturing operations. The UNS maps these levels directly into topic path segments:

| ISA-95 Level | Level # | UNS Topic Role | Example Topic Segment |
|--------------|---------|-----------------|----------------------|
| Enterprise | 4 | Root topic | `/enterprise/` |
| Site | 3-4 | Geographic grouping | `/enterprise/site/` |
| Area | 3 | Functional zone | `/enterprise/site/area/` |
| Line / Process Cell | 2 | Production unit | `/.../productionLine/` |
| Work Cell / Unit | 1-2 | Smallest operational group | `/.../workCell/` |
| Equipment / Control Module | 0-1 | Individual asset | `/.../equipment/` |

**ISA-95 levels mapped to MQTT topic function:**

```
Level 4 (Enterprise/ERP):  AcmeEnergy/ERP/inventory/overview
Level 3 (MES/MOM):         AcmeEnergy/PermianBasin/MES/productionOrder
Level 2 (Supervisory):     AcmeEnergy/PermianBasin/NorthField/supervisor/alerts
Level 1 (Control/PLC):     REDACTED
Level 0 (Sensors):         REDACTED
```

The critical architectural shift is that in the traditional Purdue Model, data flows sequentially between adjacent levels (Level 0 to Level 1 to Level 2, etc.). In a UNS, any level publishes directly to the namespace, and any level subscribes directly. The hierarchy is retained in the topic naming, but communication is no longer constrained to layer-by-layer traversal.

**Practical nuance from your project:** Your ARCHITECTURE.md already defines an ISA-95 hierarchy (Enterprise/Site/Area/Cell/Equipment) that maps directly to UNS topic generation. The `UNS Topic Builder` in your pipeline produces topics like:

```
acme-energy/permian/north/pad-12/well/e-77/telemetry
```

This is exactly the ISA-95-to-UNS mapping pattern used in production systems.

Sources: [HiveMQ - Smart Manufacturing Using ISA95, Sparkplug and UNS](https://www.hivemq.com/resources/smart-manufacturing-using-isa95-mqtt-sparkplug-and-uns/), [FlowFuse - Designing Topic Hierarchy](https://flowfuse.com/blog/2025/01/designing-topic-hierarchy-for-your-uns/), [Corso Systems - ISA-95 and Sparkplug B](https://corsosystems.com/posts/using-isa-95-and-sparkplug-b-together)

### 4. Payload Conventions -- What a UNS Message Looks Like

There is no single enforced standard, but strong conventions have emerged. Two primary approaches exist: **plain MQTT with JSON payloads** and **Sparkplug B with Protobuf payloads**.

#### 4a. Plain MQTT / JSON Payload (Most Common for Getting Started)

**Minimal sensor reading:**

```json
{
  "timestamp": "2025-01-15T14:32:00.000Z",
  "value": 25.5,
  "unit": "Celsius",
  "quality": "Good"
}
```

**Richer telemetry payload (typical convention):**

```json
{
  "timestamp": "2025-01-15T14:32:00.000Z",
  "metrics": {
    "tubing_pressure_psi": 1250.3,
    "casing_pressure_psi": 890.1,
    "oil_rate_bpd": 320.5,
    "water_cut_pct": 45.2,
    "esp_frequency_hz": 55.0,
    "esp_motor_temp_f": 285.0,
    "esp_current_amps": 32.5
  },
  "quality": "Good",
  "source": "CygNet-SCADA",
  "equipment_id": "ESP-77"
}
```

**UMH _historian format (timestamp as Unix milliseconds):**

```json
{
  "timestamp_ms": 1680698839098,
  "tubing_pressure": 1250.3,
  "casing_pressure": 890.1,
  "motor_temperature": 285.0
}
```

**Key payload conventions:**

| Field | Convention | Notes |
|-------|-----------|-------|
| `timestamp` | ISO 8601 UTC or Unix epoch milliseconds | Time of data acquisition, not receipt |
| `value` / `metrics` | Numeric or structured object | Single value or batch of related measurements |
| `unit` / `uom` | String, standardized | Always include; standardize across enterprise |
| `quality` | Enum: `Good`, `Bad`, `Uncertain` | OPC UA quality model commonly borrowed |
| `source` | String identifier | Originating system for lineage |

**Batched metrics (for report-by-exception with historical backfill):**

```json
{
  "timestamp_ms": 1680698839098,
  "batch": [
    {"timestamp_ms": 1680698835000, "value": 1248.1},
    {"timestamp_ms": 1680698837000, "value": 1249.7},
    {"timestamp_ms": 1680698839000, "value": 1250.3}
  ]
}
```

#### 4b. Envelope Pattern (What Your Project Generates)

Your project's `UNSEnvelope` model wraps the canonical payload with context -- this is the recommended enterprise pattern:

```json
{
  "topic": "acme-energy/permian/north/pad-12/well/e-77/telemetry",
  "event_time": "2025-01-15T14:32:00Z",
  "payload": { "...canonical telemetry..." },
  "context": {
    "enterprise": "AcmeEnergy",
    "site": "Permian",
    "area": "North",
    "cell": "Pad-12",
    "equipment_class": "Well",
    "equipment_id": "E-77"
  },
  "meta": { "...lineage records..." },
  "data_quality": { "rating": "Good", "flags": [] }
}
```

Sources: [FlowFuse - UNS Data Modelling](https://flowfuse.com/blog/2023/12/unified-namespace-data-modelling/), [Cedalo - UNS MQTT Implementation](https://cedalo.com/blog/uns-mqtt-implementation/), [UMH Data Modeling](https://learn.umh.app/lesson/data-modeling-in-the-unified-namespace-mqtt-kafka/)

---

### 5. The Role of Sparkplug B Specification

Sparkplug B is an Eclipse Foundation specification that adds structure, state management, and interoperability guarantees on top of plain MQTT. It does not replace MQTT -- it defines **how** to use MQTT for industrial IoT.

#### Topic Namespace

Sparkplug mandates a fixed topic format:

```
spBv1.0/{group_id}/{message_type}/{edge_node_id}/[device_id]
```

**Message types:**

| Type | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `NBIRTH` | Edge node birth certificate -- declares all metrics, types, initial values |
| `NDEATH` | Edge node death certificate -- signals node disconnection |
| `DBIRTH` | Device birth certificate -- declares device metrics |
| `DDEATH` | Device death certificate |
| `NDATA` | Node data -- changed metrics only (report-by-exception) |
| `DDATA` | Device data -- changed metrics only |
| `NCMD` | Command to a node |
| `DCMD` | Command to a device |
| `STATE` | Critical application state (e.g., primary SCADA host status) |

#### Payload Format (Protobuf, Not JSON)

Sparkplug uses Google Protocol Buffers for compact binary serialization:

```json
// JSON representation of a Sparkplug B NBIRTH payload:
{
  "timestamp": 1486144502122,
  "metrics": [
    {
      "name": "Tubing Pressure",
      "alias": 1,
      "timestamp": 1479123452194,
      "dataType": "Float",
      "value": 1250.3,
      "is_historical": false,
      "is_transient": false,
      "is_null": false,
      "properties": {
        "engUnit": {"type": "String", "value": "psi"},
        "engLow": {"type": "Float", "value": 0.0},
        "engHigh": {"type": "Float", "value": 5000.0}
      }
    },
    {
      "name": "Motor Temperature",
      "alias": 2,
      "timestamp": 1479123452194,
      "dataType": "Float",
      "value": 285.0
    }
  ],
  "seq": 0
}
```

After the BIRTH message, subsequent NDATA/DDATA messages use **aliases instead of names** to reduce payload size:

```json
{
  "timestamp": 1486144562122,
  "metrics": [
    {"alias": 1, "timestamp": 1486144562000, "dataType": "Float", "value": 1252.1}
  ],
  "seq": 3
}
```

#### How Sparkplug B Differs from Plain MQTT

| Feature | Plain MQTT | Sparkplug B |
|---------|-----------|-------------|
| Payload format | Free-form (usually JSON) | Protobuf (defined schema) |
| State management | None built-in | Birth/Death certificates |
| Metric discovery | Manual / out-of-band | Automatic via BIRTH messages |
| Data types | Implicit | Explicit (Int32, Float, Boolean, etc.) |
| Report-by-exception | Application-level | Protocol-level with sequence tracking |
| Topic structure | Free-form | Mandated namespace |
| Bandwidth efficiency | Moderate (JSON text) | High (binary + aliases) |
| Interoperability | Low (custom schemas) | High (any Sparkplug-aware consumer) |

#### The ISA-95 Mapping Problem with Sparkplug

Sparkplug provides only three customizable topic segments: `group_id`, `edge_node_id`, `device_id`. ISA-95 needs 5+ levels. Two workarounds exist:

**Parris Method** -- embed hierarchy in group_id using a delimiter:

```
spBv1.0/AcmeEnergy:Permian:NorthField:Pad12/DDATA/PLC-01/ESP-77
```

**Recommended approach** -- convert Sparkplug topics to vanilla MQTT topics at the broker level, then build the ISA-95 hierarchy in the plain MQTT namespace. This avoids forcing the equipment model into Sparkplug's constrained topic structure.

Sources: [HiveMQ - Sparkplug Payload Structures](https://www.hivemq.com/blog/mqtt-payload-structures-iiot/), [Eclipse Sparkplug 3.0 Spec](https://www.eclipse.org/tahu/spec/sparkplug_spec.pdf), [Corso Systems - ISA-95 and Sparkplug B](https://corsosystems.com/posts/using-isa-95-and-sparkplug-b-together), [Canary Labs - Sparkplug](https://blog.canarylabs.com/get-started-with-mqtt-sparkplug)

---

### 6. Key Architectural Patterns

#### 6a. Publish / Subscribe

The fundamental pattern. Publishers and subscribers are completely decoupled:

- **Publishers** (PLCs, SCADA gateways, edge devices) send data to topic paths. They do not know or care who is listening.
- **Subscribers** (dashboards, historians, analytics engines, MES) subscribe to topic patterns. They do not know or care who is publishing.
- **The broker** handles routing. This is the only integration point.

This means adding a new consumer (e.g., a machine learning pipeline) requires zero changes to any existing publisher.

#### 6b. Report-by-Exception (RBE)

Data is published only when a value changes, not on a fixed poll interval. This is fundamental to both Sparkplug B and efficient UNS operation.

**How it works:**

1. On connection, a BIRTH message publishes all current metric values (the "full state snapshot").
2. After that, only changed values are published.
3. The broker retains the last message per topic (`retained` flag), so new subscribers immediately get current state.
4. Sparkplug adds sequence numbers to detect gaps (missed messages).

**Trade-off:** Tags that legitimately do not change for long periods may appear "stale" to monitoring systems. Solutions include periodic heartbeat publishes or configuring stale-detection thresholds.

#### 6c. Birth and Death Certificates

This pattern solves a critical problem: **how does a consumer know what data a device provides, and whether the device is currently online?**

**Birth certificate (NBIRTH / DBIRTH):**

- Published when a device connects or reconnects
- Contains the complete list of metrics with names, data types, initial values, and engineering units
- Enables auto-discovery -- a new SCADA application can subscribe to `spBv1.0/+/DBIRTH/#` and automatically learn every device and metric in the system

**Death certificate (NDEATH / DDEATH):**

- Published when a device disconnects
- Uses MQTT's **Last Will and Testament (LWT)** feature: the death message is registered with the broker at connection time, and the broker publishes it automatically if the client disconnects unexpectedly (network failure, power loss)
- All subscribers instantly know the device is offline and can mark its data as stale/uncertain

**State awareness flow:**

```
1. Device connects    -> Broker publishes NBIRTH (all metrics + initial values)
2. Value changes      -> Device publishes NDATA (changed metrics only)
3. Device disconnects -> Broker publishes NDEATH (via LWT)
4. Device reconnects  -> Broker publishes NBIRTH (full state refresh)
```

Sources: [Canary Labs - Sparkplug RBE](https://blog.canarylabs.com/get-started-with-mqtt-sparkplug), [HiveMQ - Sparkplug Architecture](https://www.hivemq.com/blog/sparkplug-essentials-part-2-architecture/), [Inductive Automation Forum - RBE Tag Staleness](https://forum.inductiveautomation.com/t/mqtt-tags-go-stale-due-to-uns-report-by-exception/86590)

---

### 7. Contextualization -- Mapping Raw SCADA Tags into UNS Topics

This is the central problem your `scada_harmonization` project addresses. Raw SCADA tags carry no inherent context about where they sit in the organizational hierarchy.

#### The Problem: Raw Tags Have No Context

A typical SCADA system has flat, cryptic tag names:

```
45TT236          (plant 45, temperature transmitter, loop 236)
WELL_E77_TBG_P   (well E-77, tubing pressure)
E77.ESP.MotorTemp (dot-separated, camelCase)
csg_press_kpa    (snake_case, non-standard units)
```

These carry meaning to the person who configured them, but they are opaque to any system consuming them for cross-site analytics.

#### The Solution: A Contextualization Layer

Contextualization is the process of extracting or enriching these raw tags with:

1. **ISA-95 identity** -- which enterprise, site, area, cell, and equipment this tag belongs to
2. **Semantic meaning** -- what physical measurement this tag represents (tubing pressure, motor temperature, flow rate)
3. **Unit standardization** -- converting to a common unit system
4. **Quality assessment** -- flagging suspect or out-of-range values

#### Where Contextualization Happens

In a UNS architecture, contextualization typically occurs at the **edge gateway** or in a **transformation layer** between the raw data source and the UNS broker:

```
PLC / RTU (raw tags)
    |
    v
Edge Gateway / Adapter
    - Parses tag naming conventions
    - Maps tag to ISA-95 hierarchy
    - Converts units
    - Adds metadata (timestamp, quality, source)
    |
    v
MQTT Broker (UNS)
    - Topic: acme-energy/permian/north/pad-12/well/e-77/telemetry
    - Payload: standardized JSON with context
```

#### Concrete Mapping Example

**Raw SCADA tag from CygNet-style source:**

```
Tag:    WELL_E77_TBG_PRESS
Value:  8618.7
Unit:   kPa
Status: P
```

**Contextualized UNS output:**

```
Topic: acme-energy/permian/north/pad-12/well/e-77/telemetry

Payload:
{
  "timestamp": "2025-01-15T14:32:00Z",
  "tubing_pressure_psi": 1250.3,
  "quality": "Good",
  "lineage": {
    "tubing_pressure_psi": {
      "source_key": "WELL_E77_TBG_PRESS",
      "original_value": 8618.7,
      "conversion": "kPa_to_psi"
    }
  }
}
```

**Two-tier namespace approach (recommended):**

Some architectures maintain both a raw namespace and a contextualized namespace:

```
_raw/cygnet/WELL_E77_TBG_PRESS        <- raw data, unprocessed, ingested immediately
acme-energy/permian/north/.../telemetry <- contextualized, standardized, enterprise-ready
```

The raw namespace allows data collection from day one while the contextualization model is still being refined.

Sources: [HiveMQ - Designing UNS Semantic Hierarchy](https://www.hivemq.com/blog/designing-your-uns-semantic-information-hierarchy/), [FlowFuse - UNS Data Modelling](https://flowfuse.com/blog/2023/12/unified-namespace-data-modelling/), [i-flow - SCADA in the UNS](https://i-flow.io/en/ressources/scada-in-the-unified-namespace-uns-new-role-in-industrial-iot/)

---

### 8. Real-World UNS Topic Tree for Upstream Oil & Gas

While published examples are scarce for oil & gas specifically (most public UNS documentation uses manufacturing examples), the ISA-95 hierarchy maps naturally to upstream operations. Based on the conventions established above and oil & gas domain structure, here is a realistic topic tree:

```
acme-energy/                                          # Enterprise
  permian-basin/                                      # Site
    north-field/                                      # Area
      pad-12/                                         # Cell (well pad)
        well/                                         # Equipment Class
          e-77/                                       # Equipment ID
            telemetry/                                # Real-time measurements
              tubing-pressure
              casing-pressure
              oil-rate
              water-cut
              gas-rate
              wellhead-temperature
            status/                                   # Operating state
            alarms/                                   # Alarm events
          e-78/
            telemetry/
            status/
        esp/                                          # Equipment Class
          esp-77/                                     # Equipment ID
            telemetry/
              motor-temperature
              intake-pressure
              discharge-pressure
              vibration
              frequency
              current
              power
            status/                                   # running, tripped, idle
            alarms/                                   # high-temp, overcurrent
            performance/                              # calculated KPIs
              pump-efficiency
              head-curve-deviation
          esp-78/
            telemetry/
            status/
        separator/
          sep-12a/
            telemetry/
              oil-out-rate
              water-out-rate
              gas-out-rate
              level
              pressure
              temperature
            status/
      pad-13/
        well/
          e-80/
            ...
    south-field/                                      # Area
      pad-20/
        ...
  eagle-ford/                                         # Site
    central-block/                                    # Area
      ...
  _enterprise/                                        # Enterprise-level systems
    erp/
      production-accounting/
      lease-operating-expense/
    scada-historian/
      archive-status/
    analytics/
      field-decline-curves/
      esp-health-scores/
```

**Key design decisions for oil & gas:**

- **Pad as Cell:** A well pad is the natural equivalent of an ISA-95 work cell -- it is the smallest unit that groups related equipment.
- **Equipment class as a level:** Separating `well/`, `esp/`, `separator/` under a pad allows subscribing to all ESPs across a field with `acme-energy/permian-basin/north-field/+/esp/#`.
- **Telemetry vs. status vs. alarms:** Separate data categories as sub-topics so consumers can subscribe to exactly what they need.
- **Enterprise systems as sibling branches:** ERP, analytics, and historian data live in the same namespace but under clearly separated branches.

Sources: [HiveMQ - Oil & Gas Digital Transformation](https://www.hivemq.com/blog/digital-transformation-oil-gas-uns-mqtt-distributed-data-intelligence/), [HiveMQ - Upstream Oil & Gas Case Study](https://www.hivemq.com/case-studies/upstream-oil-and-gas/), [EMQ - MQTT in Oil & Gas](https://www.emqx.com/en/blog/application-of-mqtt-protocol-in-oil-and-gas-industry)

---

### 9. Common Pitfalls When Implementing UNS

**1. No clear business objective.** The most common failure mode. Teams implement a UNS because it is trendy without defining what business outcomes it should enable. Without a "why," initial enthusiasm fades.

**2. Lack of data governance.** Without central specifications for topic naming, payload schemas, and data ownership, the namespace degenerates into a "chaotic namespace." Different teams create inconsistent topic structures, redundant data, and incompatible payload formats. You need someone (or a team) who owns the data model.

**3. Trying to harmonize OT data without standardization at source level.** Factories and fields have historically grown, proprietary data structures with inconsistent naming. Without technical harmonization (uniform payload formats, consistent topic mapping), the UNS becomes a dumping ground. This is exactly the problem your harmonization service solves.

**4. Ignoring security from the start.** Once data is in the UNS, it is accessible to all subscribers. Access control, encryption (TLS), and authentication must be part of the initial design, not bolted on later.

**5. Forcing ISA-95 mapping into Sparkplug B's limited topic structure.** Sparkplug only provides three customizable topic segments. Embedding a 5+ level ISA-95 hierarchy using delimiters creates technical debt and parsing complexity for every consumer.

**6. Not handling "brownfield" integration.** Most industrial environments have legacy PLCs, RTUs, and protocols (Modbus, OPC DA) that cannot natively publish MQTT. Edge gateways are required, and their selection, configuration, and maintenance are a significant project in themselves.

**7. Over-engineering the topic structure before collecting any data.** Some teams spend months designing the "perfect" namespace before publishing a single message. The recommended approach: start with a raw namespace, collect data immediately, and refine the contextualized namespace iteratively.

**8. Confusing UNS with a historian or data lake.** The UNS is a real-time current-state layer. It is not a replacement for time-series storage. Historians, data lakes, and analytics systems should subscribe to the UNS and persist data according to their own retention needs.

**9. Underestimating organizational change.** UNS requires cross-functional collaboration between OT, IT, and data engineering teams. Naming conventions and data ownership disputes are often harder to resolve than technical challenges.

Sources: [i-flow - Why UNS Projects Fail](https://i-flow.io/en/ressources/6-organizational-mistakes-why-unified-namespace-uns-projects-fail-in-manufacturing-companies/), [i-flow - Lessons from the Data Lake Hype](https://i-flow.io/en/ressources/unified-namespace-lessons-from-the-data-lake-hype/), [Automation World - UNS Real-World Challenges](https://www.automationworld.com/factory/iiot/article/33016191/unified-namespace-real-world-applications-and-challenges)

---

### 10. File-Based / Batch Simulation of UNS Concepts

Your project is already a demonstration of this approach. A file-based simulation can faithfully represent all the core UNS concepts without requiring a live MQTT broker. Here is how each concept maps:

| UNS Concept | Live MQTT Implementation | File-Based Equivalent |
|-------------|------------------------|-----------------------|
| **Topic namespace** | MQTT topic string | Generated topic path in output JSON (your `UNSEnvelope.topic`) |
| **Publish** | `client.publish(topic, payload)` | Write a JSON line to `canonical.jsonl` with topic + payload |
| **Subscribe** | `client.subscribe("acme/+/+/esp/#")` | Filter/grep output JSONL by topic pattern |
| **Retained message (current state)** | Broker stores last message per topic | Python dictionary keyed by topic path (last-write-wins) |
| **Report-by-exception** | Only publish on value change | Compare incoming value against last-known value in state dict; only write if changed |
| **Birth certificate** | NBIRTH with all metrics | Initial "full snapshot" record per device in output |
| **Death certificate** | NDEATH on disconnect | Sentinel record with `"status": "offline"` and timestamp |
| **Quality flags** | `is_null`, `quality` in payload | Your `DataQuality` model (Good/Suspect/Bad + flags) |
| **Dead letter** | Error topic or separate queue | Your `dead_letter.jsonl` |
| **Wildcard subscription** | `+` and `#` in topic filter | Regex or glob matching on topic strings in output |

**Implementation pattern using a Python dictionary as an in-memory UNS:**

```python
class InMemoryUNS:
    """Simulates a UNS broker as a Python dictionary."""
    
    def __init__(self):
        self.state: dict[str, dict] = {}         # topic -> last payload (retained)
        self.subscribers: dict[str, list] = {}     # pattern -> [callback, ...]
        self.history: list[dict] = []              # ordered event log
    
    def publish(self, topic: str, payload: dict):
        """Simulate MQTT publish with retain."""
        self.state[topic] = payload                # retained message
        self.history.append({"topic": topic, "payload": payload})
        for pattern, callbacks in self.subscribers.items():
            if topic_matches(pattern, topic):
                for cb in callbacks:
                    cb(topic, payload)
    
    def subscribe(self, pattern: str, callback):
        """Simulate MQTT subscribe with wildcards."""
        self.subscribers.setdefault(pattern, []).append(callback)
        # Deliver retained messages for matching topics
        for topic, payload in self.state.items():
            if topic_matches(pattern, topic):
                callback(topic, payload)
    
    def get_current_state(self, topic: str) -> dict | None:
        """Get retained message for a topic."""
        return self.state.get(topic)
    
    def export_to_jsonl(self, path: str):
        """Persist the event log to file."""
        with open(path, "w") as f:
            for event in self.history:
                f.write(json.dumps(event) + "\n")
```

**What your project already demonstrates:**

Your pipeline (fixture files -> adapters -> canonical model -> UNS envelope -> JSONL output) is functionally equivalent to:

1. **Ingestion** = receiving published messages from multiple SCADA sources
2. **Adapters** = edge gateway contextualization (raw tags -> ISA-95 hierarchy)
3. **Canonical model** = enforcing the payload schema contract
4. **UNS Envelope** = producing the message that would be published to the broker
5. **JSONL output** = the "broker's" persistent event log
6. **Dead letter** = the error/rejection queue

To make the UNS simulation more explicit, you could add:
- A state dictionary that maintains "current value" per topic (simulating MQTT retained messages)
- A report-by-exception filter that compares each incoming value against the retained state and only emits if changed
- A birth/death event generator that produces initial full-state snapshots and offline sentinel records

Sources: [GitHub - mkashwin/unifiednamespace](https://github.com/mkashwin/unifiednamespace), [Cedalo - UNS MQTT Implementation](https://cedalo.com/blog/uns-mqtt-implementation/)

# SCADA Harmonization & Contextualization Service
## Product Requirements Document (PRD)

---

## 1. Overview

This project implements a standalone industrial data harmonization service that ingests heterogeneous SCADA telemetry events and produces standardized, ISA-95-aligned canonical telemetry messages suitable for enterprise analytics and Unified Namespace (UNS) streaming architectures.

The system simulates a real brownfield harmonization program where multiple legacy operational systems publish semantically inconsistent telemetry data — the kind of integration friction encountered when consolidating acquisitions (e.g., Pioneer/CygNet, Denbury/Wonderware) into a unified enterprise platform.

This project is intentionally designed to:

- Apply ISA-95 Part 2 for physical equipment hierarchy
- Standardize naming conventions and units
- Normalize status encodings
- Enforce canonical telemetry contracts
- Provide lineage and explainability
- Produce robust error handling and dead-letter routing

**Pydantic is a first-class architectural concern.** The project uses Pydantic extensively as both the validation engine and the modeling framework. Every data boundary — source ingestion, intermediate extraction, canonical validation, UNS envelope construction, error reporting — is enforced by a Pydantic model. This makes the project a practical vehicle for learning advanced Pydantic features including discriminated unions, field/model validators, aliases, custom types, constrained fields, and serializers.

---

## 2. Problem Statement

Industrial telemetry systems often suffer from:

- **Inconsistent naming conventions:** camelCase, snake_case, hyphenated keys (e.g., `PUMP_01_TEMP` vs `P-101.T` vs `pump-1-temperature`)
- **Different JSON shapes:** flat vs nested vs topic-based identity
- **Different units:** bpd vs m³/day, psi vs kPa, °F vs °C
- **Inconsistent status encodings:** "P", "RUN", "Producing", "ONLINE"
- **Unreliable timestamps:** ISO strings, epoch seconds, epoch milliseconds, missing
- **Lack of contextual hierarchy:** no ISA-95 alignment, no standard asset model

This is compounded during M&A integration, where acquired companies bring entirely different SCADA platforms (CygNet, Wonderware, FactoryTalk) with proprietary tag structures and naming conventions. Without harmonization, the "metadata problem" makes raw tags useless for enterprise analytics and AI/ML applications.

These issues prevent:

- Cross-site KPI standardization
- Enterprise-level analytics and AI applications
- Reliable streaming architectures (UNS)
- M&A system integration (the primary business driver)
- Trustworthy predictive maintenance and autonomous control

---

## 3. Goals

The system must:

1. Ingest events from 3 heterogeneous source types representing different legacy SCADA platforms
2. Support multiple equipment classes (Wells and ESPs at minimum)
3. Extract ISA-95 contextual hierarchy from each source's naming convention
4. Normalize units and statuses to canonical standards
5. Validate telemetry constraints (type, range, cross-field consistency)
6. Emit canonical enterprise-aligned events via Pydantic models
7. Publish UNS-compatible topic structures
8. Provide per-field mapping lineage metadata
9. Produce structured error outputs with dead-letter routing for invalid events
10. Score data quality for each canonical event

---

## 4. Non-Goals

This system does NOT:

- Connect to real MQTT brokers or OPC UA servers
- Implement a full historian or time-series database
- Perform persistent storage beyond local JSONL files
- Replace SCADA systems or PLCs
- Implement real-time streaming (batch/file-based processing only)
- Perform fuzzy/AI-assisted tag matching (deterministic mapping only)

It is a contextualization and harmonization layer only.

---

## 5. Functional Requirements

### 5.1 Multi-Source Ingestion

The system must support three source types that represent realistic legacy SCADA platforms with different naming conventions, JSON shapes, and engineering units.

**Source A — CygNet-style legacy flat JSON:**

Flat key-value pairs using underscore-delimited compound names. Imperial units. Status as short codes.

```json
{
  "tag": "PERMIAN_NORTH_PAD12_WELL_E77",
  "flow": 1250.5,
  "pressure": 3200.0,
  "temp": 185.0,
  "status": "P",
  "ts": "2024-03-15T14:30:00Z"
}
```

**Source B — Wonderware-style legacy flat JSON:**

Different key names, metric units (m³/day, kPa, °C), verbose status strings, epoch timestamps.

```json
{
  "wellId": "E-77",
  "site": "Permian",
  "area": "North",
  "pad": "Pad-12",
  "flowRate_m3d": 198.8,
  "tubingPressure_kPa": 22063.0,
  "temperature_c": 85.0,
  "wellStatus": "Producing",
  "timestamp": 1710513000
}
```

**Source C — Ignition/MQTT UNS-style nested JSON:**

Hierarchical structure with topic-embedded identity. Mixed units. Epoch milliseconds.

```json
{
  "topic": "Exxon/Permian/North/Pad-12/ESP/E-77/telemetry",
  "payload": {
    "intake_pressure_psi": 1850.0,
    "motor_temp_f": 275.0,
    "motor_amps": 42.5,
    "vibration_ips": 0.35,
    "status": "RUN"
  },
  "timestamp_ms": 1710513000000
}
```

### 5.2 Equipment Classes

The system must support at minimum two equipment classes to demonstrate that the canonical model is genuinely generic:

**Well telemetry:**
- flow_rate_bpd (barrels per day)
- tubing_pressure_psi
- temperature_f
- status

**ESP (Electric Submersible Pump) telemetry:**
- intake_pressure_psi
- motor_temperature_f
- motor_current_amps
- vibration_ips (inches per second)
- status

### 5.3 Canonical Model

The canonical telemetry event must include:

**ISA-95 Identity:**
- `enterprise` (string, required)
- `site` (string, required)
- `area` (string, required)
- `cell` (string, required — the pad or unit)
- `equipment_class` (enum: `Well`, `ESP`)
- `equipment_id` (string, required)

**Telemetry Measurements:**
- Equipment-class-specific measurement fields (see 5.2)
- All measurements normalized to canonical units (imperial)

**Event Metadata:**
- `event_time` (timezone-aware UTC datetime, required)
- `status` (enum: `Producing` / `ShutIn` / `Offline` / `Unknown`)
- `data_quality` (structured — see 5.9)

**Lineage:**
- `meta.source_system` (which source type produced this event)
- `meta.source_event_id` (hash or identifier of the original payload)
- `meta.field_lineage` (per-field mapping: source key, original value, conversion applied)

### 5.4 ISA-95 Alignment

The canonical identity must follow ISA-95 Part 2 hierarchy:

```
Enterprise → Site → Area → Cell → Equipment Class → Equipment ID
```

Each source adapter must extract this hierarchy from the source's own naming convention — whether that's a compound tag name (Source A), discrete fields (Source B), or a topic path (Source C).

### 5.5 Unit Normalization

Convert to canonical imperial units:

| Source Unit | Canonical Unit | Conversion |
|-------------|---------------|------------|
| m³/day      | bpd           | × 6.28981  |
| kPa         | psi           | × 0.145038 |
| °C          | °F            | × 9/5 + 32 |

Conversions must be deterministic and recorded in field lineage.

### 5.6 Status Normalization

Map all source status codes to a canonical enum:

| Canonical Status | Source A | Source B      | Source C |
|------------------|----------|---------------|----------|
| Producing        | "P"      | "Producing"   | "RUN"    |
| ShutIn           | "S"      | "ShutIn"      | "STOP"   |
| Offline          | "X"      | "Offline"     | "OFF"    |
| Unknown          | (any other) | (any other) | (any other) |

Unmapped status codes must resolve to `Unknown` (not raise an error).

### 5.7 Timestamp Handling

Accept:
- ISO 8601 strings (with or without timezone)
- Epoch seconds (integer or float)
- Epoch milliseconds (integer)

Normalize to timezone-aware UTC datetime. Naive ISO strings must be assumed UTC. Missing timestamps must trigger a validation error (dead-letter).

### 5.8 Validation Constraints

The canonical model must enforce:

**Type constraints:**
- All measurement fields must be numeric (float)
- All identity fields must be non-empty strings
- Status must be a valid enum member
- Event time must be a valid datetime

**Range constraints:**
- `flow_rate_bpd` >= 0
- `tubing_pressure_psi` >= 0 and <= 15000
- `temperature_f` >= -40 and <= 500
- `intake_pressure_psi` >= 0 and <= 10000
- `motor_current_amps` >= 0
- `vibration_ips` >= 0

**Cross-field constraints:**
- `Producing` status with `flow_rate_bpd == 0` should flag `data_quality` as `Suspect` (not reject)
- Missing optional measurement fields are allowed but must be reflected in `data_quality`

### 5.9 Data Quality

Each canonical event must include a structured `data_quality` assessment:

- `quality` (enum: `Good` / `Suspect` / `Bad`)
- `flags` (list of strings describing any issues detected)

Examples of flags:
- `"zero_flow_while_producing"` — status is Producing but flow rate is zero
- `"coerced_status_to_unknown"` — original status was not in the mapping
- `"missing_optional_field:vibration_ips"` — an optional measurement was absent
- `"timestamp_assumed_utc"` — naive ISO string was treated as UTC

### 5.10 UNS Output

**Topic format:**

```
{enterprise}/{site}/{area}/{cell}/{equipment_class}/{equipment_id}/telemetry
```

All topic segments must be lowercase, with spaces replaced by hyphens and special characters stripped.

**Output envelope:**

```json
{
  "topic": "exxon/permian/north/pad-12/well/e-77/telemetry",
  "event_time": "2024-03-15T14:30:00+00:00",
  "payload": { },
  "context": {
    "enterprise": "Exxon",
    "site": "Permian",
    "area": "North",
    "cell": "Pad-12",
    "equipment_class": "Well",
    "equipment_id": "E-77"
  },
  "meta": {
    "source_system": "source_a",
    "source_event_id": "abc123...",
    "field_lineage": { }
  },
  "data_quality": {
    "quality": "Good",
    "flags": []
  }
}
```

### 5.11 Error Handling and Dead-Letter Routing

Invalid events must:

- Produce structured validation errors (leveraging Pydantic's `ValidationError`)
- Be routed to `dead_letter.jsonl`
- Include:
  - Failure reason (list of field-level errors)
  - Original payload snapshot
  - Source system identifier
  - Timestamp of processing attempt

```json
{
  "error_id": "...",
  "source_system": "source_b",
  "timestamp": "2024-03-15T14:31:00+00:00",
  "errors": [
    {
      "field": "event_time",
      "message": "Missing required field: timestamp",
      "type": "missing"
    }
  ],
  "original_payload": { }
}
```

---

## 6. Success Criteria

The system successfully:

- Processes mixed events from all three sources and both equipment classes
- **Produces identical canonical output regardless of source** — the same physical event arriving via Source A and Source B yields the same canonical telemetry
- Converts units correctly (verified by round-trip tolerance tests)
- Normalizes statuses correctly across all source mappings
- Rejects malformed payloads with clear, structured error messages
- Produces deterministic, sanitized UNS topics
- Tracks per-field lineage for every canonical event
- Scores data quality with meaningful flags

---

## 7. Acceptance Testing

### 7.1 Unit Tests
- Unit conversion functions pass (with tolerance for floating-point)
- Status mapping covers all source codes plus unknown fallback
- Timestamp parsing handles ISO, epoch seconds, epoch milliseconds, and missing
- Range validators reject out-of-bounds values
- Data quality flags fire for cross-field inconsistencies

### 7.2 Integration Tests
- Valid fixtures from each source produce correct canonical events
- Broken fixtures produce dead-letter entries with meaningful error messages
- End-to-end pipeline: raw source JSON → adapter → transform → canonical → UNS envelope

### 7.3 Cross-Source Equivalence Tests
- The same physical event represented in Source A and Source B format produces **identical** canonical output (the core proof that harmonization works)

### 7.4 Edge Case Tests
- Missing optional fields are handled gracefully (not rejected)
- Null values in required fields produce dead-letter entries
- Out-of-range values produce dead-letter entries with specific field errors
- Empty payloads, malformed JSON structures
- Duplicate events (same event_time + equipment_id)

### 7.5 Output Validation
- Canonical JSONL output is valid, line-delimited JSON
- Dead-letter JSONL output contains original payload and structured errors
- UNS topics are lowercase, hyphenated, and deterministic
